text: The “employment- related practices” exclusion in Employer's personal injury liability policy did not apply because the defamation was not directed to plaintiff's performance during employment. [Golden Eagle Ins. Corp. v. Rocky Cola Café, Inc., supra, 94 CA4th at 128, 114 CR2d at 22] [3:395 - 3:399] Reserved. 2) [3:400] Broad interpretation: Other courts find post-termination defamation “employment related” if it would not have occurred but for the employment. Under this view, it is enough that the defamatory remark's content was “directed to [employee's] performance during employment.” [Frank & Freedus v. Allstate Ins. Co., supra, 45 CA4th at 471-472, 52 CR2d at 684; Loyola Marymount Univ. v. Hartford Acc. & Indem. Co. (1990) 219 CA3d 1217, 1223, 271 CR 528, 530] • [3:401] A defamation claim based on the employer's post-termination statement to other employees explaining the reason plaintiff had been fired was “clearly employment related” because the employer was attempting to boost the morale of the other employees.
